headline: Family is defined by bonds, not biology—chosen connections can be as powerful as blood
universal_truth: Belonging is a fundamental need that can be met in many ways
fun_facts: The concept of 'nuclear family' is historically recent—extended families were the norm for most of human history
Children raised in loving environments thrive regardless of family structure
Many cultures consider close friends as family—language often has words for 'chosen siblings'
discussion_questions: Who do you consider family beyond blood relatives?
How has your definition of family changed over time?
What makes a bond feel like family?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: The word 'family' might conjure parents and siblings. But look closer: family is really about connection, support, and belonging. Adopted children, chosen friends, created communities—family is defined by bonds, not just biology.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: If family can mean many things, what actually makes a family? Is it shared DNA? Living together? Legal ties? Or something harder to define but easier to feel?

options.text: Mutual commitment, support, and a sense of belonging—regardless of biology
options.response: Yes. Research shows that love, commitment, and stability matter more than family structure.

options.text: Shared genetics and legal relationships form the foundation
options.response: These can create family, but many families exist without them...

q1.title: Recent Invention
q1.script: The 'nuclear family'—two parents and their children, living alone—is historically unusual. For most of human history, extended families, multigenerational households, and community-raising of children was normal. Our current model is the exception.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Recent Invention"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: What Matters
q2.script: Decades of research show that children thrive based on love, stability, and support—not family structure. Single parents, same-sex parents, grandparents, adopted families—the form matters less than the function.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Chosen Family
q3.script: Many cultures recognize 'chosen family'—bonds as strong as blood, formed through choice and commitment. These relationships can provide the same psychological benefits as biological family. You can build family as well as inherit it.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Belonging is a need, and family is how we meet it. But the form is flexible. You can receive family, create family, and choose family. What matters is the connection, not the category.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 91—welcome to April's Mind & Skills month! Tomorrow, we'll explore how we understand each other. Until then, appreciate the family you have—however you define it.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Family Inventory - Who Belongs to You?
growTrack.learning_objective: Recognize and appreciate your actual support network
growTrack.activity: Make a list of your 'family'—not just blood relatives, but everyone who provides you belonging, support, and connection. Who shows up for you? Who do you show up for? This is your real family, whatever the labels.
